item.title: McCorkle: Ten Commandments bill won’t actually do much
item.description: A bill at the Statehouse (H. 4762) that would require the Ten Commandments in every South Carolina classroom jumped its first hurdle on Jan. 21 when a House Judiciary subcommittee favorably approved it to the full committee for consideration. The post McCorkle: Ten Commandments bill won’t actually do much appeared first on Charleston City Paper.

item.title: Settlement offers living conditions reforms at juvenile center
item.description: A five-year civil lawsuit over the living conditions at the Charleston County Juvenile Detention Center (CCJDC) has ended with a settlement that outlines reforms for the facility. item.title: Review: Passion, pragmatism square off in Austen’s sister act
item.description: Resplendent silk and burnished wood. Frothy quips and impossible curls. item.title: Burial site controversy continues for CofC dorm site
item.description: A longtime House member of a key legislative committee has raised concern about the College of Charleston’s plans to build a dormitory on an 18th century burial ground near the campus. item.title: Blotter: An odd selection
item.description: Security footage from a Mount Pleasant pharmacy on Jan. 25 captured a woman grabbing bleach, paper towels, a mop cleaning set and a blender. She then left the store without paying. Now, all of the cleaning gear makes sense — but what are you going to do with that blender? And why was all that nearly $300?
